title: Network permission, release signing, component library and the offline test for US-01-01

question:
How should US-01-01 handle the network permission, release signing, the component library and the offline test? I propose the four points below as they stand.

Done on feature/US-01-01 (WIP 4462e0c): minSdk 31, the TC-01-01 Maestro flow, and the platform versions in README.md. The rest needs your call.

The debug build that yarn stack and CI test loads its JavaScript from Metro over a local socket, and Android refuses that without INTERNET. TC-01-02 steps 2 and 3 expect the category screen and a card. Those arrive with US-02-01 and US-03-01, so that test case cannot pass in this story.

- Network: INTERNET is removed from the release build only, through a release manifest written by a config plugin; the debug build keeps it for Metro. Criterion 3 is proven by a unit test on that manifest and by aapt on a built release APK.
- Signing: the release build reads the keystore path, alias and passwords from Gradle properties KQ_UPLOAD_* in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties or the environment. Without them it fails instead of signing with the debug key.
- Component library: none. React Native core components with the app's own black and white theme tokens, written into constitution.md Stack (DEC-07 allows none).
- Offline test: criterion 4 is proven now by a derived test AC-01-01-4 (airplane mode on, the app opens its first screen). The TC-01-02 flow is written once the category screen and cards exist (US-03-01).

a) Take all four points as proposed — yarn stack and CI stay on the debug build. The shipped APK has no network permission, checked by a unit test and on the release APK. TC-01-02 runs from US-03-01; until then criterion 4 rests on the derived test. (recommended)
b) As a, but no INTERNET in any build and e2e on the release build — The tested app is exactly the shipped one. But yarn stack and the acceptance script switch to a release build with the bundle embedded: no Metro or live reload, longer CI builds, and the foundation's start command changes.
c) As a, but leave the component library to US-02-01 — The first real screen chooses it with its design in view. constitution.md Stack stays open until then, and this story makes no UI choice.

Why a: It meets NFR-05 for the APK that reaches the Kompakt without changing the foundation's start command or CI. It adds no dependency and leaves every reviewed test case untouched.

title: Upload key variables in the environment win over Gradle properties of the same name

question:
When a KQ_UPLOAD_* signing value is set both in the environment and in ~/.gradle/gradle.properties, should the environment win?

Review found that the acceptance run passes a throwaway key through KQ_UPLOAD_* environment variables, but the build read gradle.properties first. On your machine, where the real upload key sits in gradle.properties as the README says, the test build was signed with the real key and the signature check failed.

DEC-44 allows both sources but does not say which wins. Your normal release build, with values only in gradle.properties, is unchanged under either option.

a) Environment wins over gradle.properties (implemented) — A key passed in for one build, like the acceptance run's throwaway key, is always used and your real key is never touched by tests. Unit-tested and documented in the README. Cost: a stray KQ_UPLOAD_* exported in your shell would override your real key for a release build. (recommended)
b) gradle.properties wins; tests pass the throwaway with -P — Keeps the old precedence. The acceptance run passes the throwaway key's path and password on the gradlew command line, so its random throwaway password is briefly visible in the process list, which the reviewer asked to avoid.

Why a: A value given explicitly for one build should beat a persistent default; it keeps the real key out of every test build and passwords off the command line, and your normal release setup behaves exactly as before.

title: Content data format for the decks, and how US-01-02 proves its criteria

question:
May the 3+ deck use the content data format and the proof approach below, so that 4+ and 5+ follow the same format?
The constitution says the tech lead approves changes to the content data schema, and this story creates that schema. US-01-03, US-01-04, MOD-02 and MOD-03 will all be built on it. Nothing in the deck is written yet. A draft of the shape is in src/content/deck.ts on the branch.
- Format: one file per category, src/content/decks/3-plus.json, holding schemaVersion 1, category "3+" and 50 questions. Each question has a stable id, a kind (educational, popular-science, nature or trivia), pl and en each with one question and one answer string, and an optional illustration file name.
- Adding a category: add its JSON file plus one import line in src/content/decks/index.ts, inside the content folder. Screens read categories only through src/content, so no screen changes. A test fails if a deck file is not registered.
- Criterion 7 (nothing downloaded): TC-01-02 needs the category screen and cards, so as in DEC-44 it runs in US-03-01. For now a derived test AC-01-02-7 checks that the release APK's embedded bundle contains the 3+ deck and that the content code has no network calls.
- Criterion 4 (age-suitability record): the check of every question is kept in docs/delivery/content-checks/US-01-02-3-plus.md, one row per question with the four Q29 checks, and copied into the PR. A unit test fails if any question has no row with all four checks passed.
a) Take all four points as proposed | The deck and its checks are built as described. 4+ and 5+ reuse the format unchanged. Content reaches the screen in MOD-02 and MOD-03. Lowest effort, and nothing auto-discovered.
b) As proposed, but category files are discovered automatically | A new category is only a new JSON file, with no import line. This relies on Metro's require.context and needs a workaround to run in Jest, which adds setup that is harder to follow.
c) As proposed, but the age check lives only in the PR description | No record file and no test for it. The check is visible only on GitHub and nothing stops a later edit from adding an unchecked question.
→ a
It follows the story's technical notes exactly, keeps every check enforced by a test, and adds no tooling. A new category costs one obvious line next to its data file.

title: 3+ questions with a possible near-miss answer are asked as either/or
3+ questions with a possible near-miss answer are asked as either/or

question:
Should 3+ questions name two options in the question text (either/or) or stay open, given the must MOD-03-U02 says the card has no answer choices?

All 50 questions in the 3+ deck now pass the one-answer rule; CI is green and both reviewers accept the content. 46 of them get there by naming two options in the question text (What colour is a lemon: blue or yellow?); 4 stay open (3p-02, 3p-07, 3p-13, 3p-36). The card has no buttons: the options are only in the words.

The reviewers read spoken either/or text as arguably not an answer-choice UI. But MOD-03-U02 (must) says no buttons, choices or score on the card, and DSC-04-04, SRC-01-17 and SRC-01-18 rule out answer choices and a classic quiz. Which reading holds is a judgement on a must, so it is yours.

The cost of either/or: a guessing child is right half the time and the wrong option is often absurd (a spoon for brushing teeth), so 46 of 50 questions are near-trivial. Open questions were dropped because three review rounds kept finding near-miss answers a child could give (a neck warmer for a scarf, a hood for an umbrella).

- The form of the 3+ questions: either/or in the question text, or open questions.
- Whether that form also binds the 4+ and 5+ decks (US-01-03, US-01-04), or each of those stories decides its own.

a) Keep either/or for 3+; 4+ and 5+ decide their own form — The deck merges as it is (46 either/or, 4 open) and DEC-47 is confirmed for 3+ only, reading MOD-03-U02 as no choice controls on the card. Cost: 46 near-trivial questions; US-01-03 and US-01-04 face the same question again.
b) Keep either/or for 3+ and use it for 4+ and 5+ too — The deck merges as it is and US-01-03/04 follow the same rule: one form across the app, no repeat of the near-miss problem. Cost: every deck becomes a 50% guess with two options, closer to the classic quiz SRC-01-18 says the app is not.
c) Back to open questions for 3+, under a stricter near-miss rule — Open questions return, starting from the wording the reviewers accepted; each one with a near miss is reworded to rule it out, and the record names the near miss checked per row. No either/or, a literal fit with MOD-03-U02; 4+/5+ stay open too. Cost: one more content and review round. (recommended)
d) Open by default; either/or only where no rewording removes a near miss — Most questions open as in c; the few that cannot be made unambiguous keep two options, each listed with its reason in the record. Fewer rewrites than c, but those cards still carry choices, so MOD-03-U02 is bent for them.

Why c: It reads MOD-03-U02 and SRC-01-17/18 as written, and it keeps the questions worth asking: a 50% guess against an absurd option teaches little. The near-miss problem is a writing problem the record can control row by row, not a reason to change what a card is.

title: Category screen: order by age, and the 3+, 4+, 5+ checks before 4+ and 5+ ship
Category screen: order by age

question:
Can US-02-01 merge showing only 3+ (the one deck shipped), with 4+, 5+ and the full TC-02-01/02 check deferred to US-01-03 and US-01-04?

The must MOD-02-F02 says the screen lists 3+, 4+ and 5+, and TC-02-01 and TC-02-02 expect three entries. Only the 3+ deck exists today (US-01-02). 4+ and 5+ come with US-01-03 and US-01-04.

The screen builds its list from the shipped decks, sorted by age, so 4+ and 5+ will appear with no code change. The same flows will then check all three. The story's edge case already says only 3+ shows while it is the only deck. Details: DEC-48 in docs/specs/DECISIONS.md.

a) Merge now with 3+ only; full check when 4+ and 5+ land — CI runs TC-02-01/02 on every PR and expects every shipped deck in age order, so the 4+ and 5+ PRs cannot merge unless their deck shows. A line naming TC-02-01/02 as their evidence is added to US-01-03 and US-01-04. Until then MOD-02-F02 is proven for 3+ only. (recommended)
b) Hold US-02-01 until US-01-03 and US-01-04 have merged — The 4+ and 5+ decks go first, and this story then merges with TC-02-01/02 passing in full. Cost: US-02-02, US-02-03 and US-03-01 to US-03-04 all depend on US-02-01 and wait behind two content stories of 50 checked questions each.

Why a: What is missing is content, not screen code: the screen already lists whatever decks ship, youngest first. CI re-runs TC-02-01/02 on every PR, so 4+ and 5+ cannot land without passing them, and the whole category and card work is not held up.
